title: The notice step of RWB-E5-001 has no declared owner for the notice and template rows, no operation name for the two consumed calls, no case-move operation, no requirement id, and one conflict between "no person in the path" and the built D7.1 approval
source: Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP table rows DP-03, DP-13, DP-19 and section R5.4; the metadata rows of RWB-S4-E5001-APP (Depends on (build) = RWB-S4-E5001-CON, RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, RWB-PLT-N001-CON; Contract dependencies = None; Integration dependencies = None; External dependencies = None); _work/msr/context/S4.md (service row; ownership rows owned by S4: tables hearing and legal_action only; REST operations provided include POST /notices/{noticeId}/approve; events 0; workflows 1); legacy RWB-E5-001 Data table (notice DF-LEG-015 to DF-LEG-023, template DF-REF-045 to DF-REF-051, recovery_case, decision_log_entry, rule_row); TSD S4 v2 T3.1 (no notice and no template table) and T5.2 ("P6 for notices"); FSD S4 v3 A2.1; FSD P6 v3 (scope letters, notices, proof of delivery; dispatch JOB-10; notice types DEMAND and RECALL); Epic 2 master RWB-E2-014 (D7.1 approval of a demand or recall notice)
section: Sections 2, 3, 4, 12.1, 12.2, 12.7, 12.8, 13 and 19 of RWB-S4-E5001-APP; the metadata table and the fragment
description: Six values the app story needs have no single source statement, and one of them is a conflict. (1) The owner of the notice row (DF-LEG-015 to DF-LEG-023) and of the template rows (DF-REF-045 to DF-REF-051): TSD S4 T3.1 defines only legal_action and hearing, the S4 ownership rows name only those two tables, yet POST /notices/{noticeId}/approve is listed as an operation of S4 and the legacy data table puts the notice row in the story. (2) The operation name of the notice generate and send call: TSD S4 T5.2 names P6 as the notice module and no source names the operation. (3) The name of the case-move answer: no source names a published operation that moves a case state on behalf of a stage. (4) The requirement id: the legacy master carries no requirement row and the plan records reqs = [], while FSD S4 gives REQ-S4-001 for exactly this feature. (5) The template condition of R-LIT-03 (template_status = current for product and notice_type) needs template reference data, but DP-07 is not in the story's pattern set, so no reference-data contract row exists and no template table may be read in rwb_litigation. (6) The conflict: legacy AC1 says the notices are produced and sent "with no person in the path" and the FSD role table says the feature runs unattended, while the D7.1 approval of a generated demand or recall notice is a built Epic 2 capability (RWB-E2-014) on the very operation the Ownership Map gives to S4. A reader of the metadata alone would conclude that the step needs only its own contract and two platform contracts and owns the notice itself.
evidence: Context pack S4: ownership rows owned by S4 list Tables (2) hearing and legal_action, REST operations provided (5) including POST /notices/{noticeId}/approve, Events (0), Jobs (0), Workflows (1); TSD S4 v2 T3.1 defines legal_action (DF-LEG-001 to DF-LEG-014) and hearing (DF-LEG-024 to DF-LEG-029) and no notice or template object; TSD S4 v2 T5.2 states the module reaches P3 for the case, P7 for the decision log, P4 for access and reference data, P5 for documents and P6 for notices; FSD P6 v3 module scope is letters, notices, SMS, LINE, proof of delivery, with JOB-10 at 16:00 writing the WIN file and notice types DEMAND and RECALL; FSD S4 v3 A2.1.3.1 carries R-LIT-03 and VR-S4-001-1 only; the legacy story lists POST /api/recovery/v1/notices/{noticeId}/approve (Litigation A) and POST /api/recovery/v1/cases/{caseId}/legal-actions (Litigation C) and no other endpoint; the pattern set of the slice is DP03, DP13, DP19 and neither DP-06, DP-07 nor DP-09 is in it; the metadata C row is None
area: Dependency map, object ownership and contract surface, S4 rwb-litigation with P6 rwb-comms, P3 rwb-case, P7 rwb-decision and the reference-data owner
owner_role: Solution architect, S4 rwb-litigation, with the P6 rwb-comms, P3 rwb-case and P7 rwb-decision architects and the reference-data owner
proposed: Carry the two consumed calls as non-blocking C rows in the Dependency Map (the P6 notice generate and send, the rwb-case stage answer) and add DP-07 to the pattern set of the key if a template read is wanted, or keep the template fact on the P6 contract as the story does; record the notice and template rows as P6's in the Ownership Map or correct the S4 row if the intent was that S4 owns them; name the P6 operation and the case answer in those services' contract stories when they are written; add REQ-S4-001 to the trace of the key and decide once, in the PRD of EP05, whether the D7.1 approval gates this step.

title: The contract baseline of the notice step fixes three operations and two consumed calls whose notice and template ownership, operation names, case answer and requirement id no source states, and the D7.1 approval is declared without a decision on whether it gates the step
source: Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP table rows DP-03, DP-13, DP-19 and section R5.4; the metadata rows of RWB-S4-E5001-CON (all three dependency rows None); _work/msr/context/S4.md service row and ownership rows; TSD S4 v2 T-A.1 (API-S4-001 to API-S4-005) and T6.1; FSD P6 v3; Epic 2 master RWB-E2-014; legacy RWB-E5-001
section: Sections 2, 3, 12.1, 12.2, 12.7, 12.8 and 19 of RWB-S4-E5001-CON; the metadata table and the fragment
description: The contract half has to declare a surface that the sources only partly describe. The notice and template rows named in the consumed row have no owner in TSD S4 and no owner row for S4 in the Ownership Map, while the approve operation that touches the notice is S4's. The generate and send operation of rwb-comms and the case-move answer have no name in any source. The reference-data route for the template (DP-07's H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON and C RWB-P3-E1043-CON) is absent from the pattern set, so the baseline consumes the template fact on the notice contract instead and declares no reference-data dependency. The requirement id is absent from the legacy master. The D7.1 approval of a generated notice is a built capability and its gate status is not stated, so the baseline names the operation without deciding the gate. The baseline is buildable on Day 1 against fakes and the placeholders are marked in the document, so nothing blocks; the exposure is a baseline that another team cannot reconcile with the Ownership Map without the assumptions below.
evidence: The metadata rows of RWB-S4-E5001-CON name None for build, contract, integration and external dependencies; the pattern set is DP03, DP13, DP19; TSD S4 v2 T-A.1 lists API-S4-001 POST /notices/{noticeId}/approve and API-S4-004 and API-S4-005 on the legal action and no notice read or template read; TSD S4 v2 T3.1 defines no notice and no template object; the context pack lists two S4 tables and five S4 operations including the notice approval; FSD P6 v3 gives the notice, its templates and the dispatch to P6; Architecture v5 slide 19 gives the S4 IN row NoticeDelivered only; the Ownership Map publishes no rwb-comms or rwb-case operation for this key
area: Contract surface and dependency map, S4 rwb-litigation with P6 rwb-comms, P3 rwb-case and the reference-data owner
owner_role: Solution architect, S4 rwb-litigation, with the P6 rwb-comms, P3 rwb-case and reference-data owners
proposed: Record the two consumed rows as C dependencies with their placeholders in the Dependency Map; declare the notice and template ownership in the Ownership Map (P6) and name the P6 operations in its contract story; keep the template status on the notice contract or add DP-07 consciously; add REQ-S4-001 to the trace; and decide the D7.1 gate in the EP05 PRD before the baseline is frozen.
